text.p: The stocks of U.S. Robotics Corp. and 3Com Corp. were the most active in heavy Nasdaq trading Thursday after their announcement that 3Com would buy U.S. Robotics in a stock swap valued at $6.6 billion.
3Com, a Santa Clara, Calif.-based maker of computer network equipment, and U.S. Robotics, which makes computer modems, announced the deal late Wednesday after the stock markets closed.
3Com's stock dropped $3 to $36, with more than 12 million shares traded. U.S. Robotics, which rose $2 to $63, was the second most-heavily traded issue, with nearly 10 million shares changing hands.

The combination of the two firms would create the second-biggest computer network company after San Jose, Calif.-based Cisco Systems Inc. Cisco's stock dropped $1.25 to $56.875 in heavy trading on Nasdaq.
Under the deal, 3Com would swap 1.75 shares for each share of Skokie, Ill.-based U.S. Robotics. The deal was valued at $6.6 billion based on Tuesday's closing price of $39.125 per 3Com share.
